title: parse_playlist passes av_strlcpy a SOURCE length where its contract takes the DESTINATION size, so a long #EXT-X-KEY URI overruns key_uri
object: VariantStream, one allocation holding key_file, key_uri, key_string and iv_string adjacently (libavformat/hlsenc.c:174-178)
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: av_strlcpy(dst, src, size) writes at most size-1 bytes of src plus a NUL, and size is the DESTINATION's size; `end - ptr` is the source's length, which the playlist chooses, so a URI longer than key_uri licenses a copy past it
allocator_layer: the object IS one allocation and the crossing is interior to it. There is no inner allocator and nothing sub-allocated the crossed region, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT NESTED. Recorded explicitly because the tally is per corpus and case.json carries no nested field.
fidelity: real allocator, model consumer, and a faithful av_strlcpy. The buffers are REDUCED from LINE_BUFFER_SIZE + 1 == 4097 to 64: the defect is that a destination-size argument receives a source length, so what matters is that the length can exceed the destination, not the destination's absolute size. av_strlcpy is NOT reduced -- it is the function whose contract is misused, so reducing it would hide the bug.
live_proof: read from the PINNED source: n9.0.1:libavformat/hlsenc.c contains the FIXED form `FFMIN(end - ptr + 1, sizeof(vs->key_uri))` (1 occurrence) and the pre-fix `av_strlcpy(vs->key_uri, ptr, end - ptr)` 0 times. Two-sided. A fix-reversal.
distinguishing: the magnitude is ATTACKER-CHOSEN rather than fixed by a type's length -- the playlist supplies it -- which is what separates this from cases 3, 5 and 8. The upstream hunk also switches the delimiter search from "," to '"'; that is a separate truncation fix in the same hunk and is NOT part of this crossing, which PROVENANCE.md states so the arm is not credited with it.

spatial.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-capstone/: **NOT CAUGHT; the defect reproduced**: the sequence completed with the crossing made, which the case's own CHECKs place inside ONE allocation, so an allocation-granular bound is in bounds for it. WHAT THIS IMAGE CANNOT SEPARATE: av_malloc and av_refstruct_allocz here are the buffer-pool port's arena carve (ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/src/shared/metadata-allocator.c), which returns an interior pointer carrying the whole metadata arena's bounds, so no per-allocation bound exists in this image at all. The completion is fixed twice over -- the case's CHECKs keep the crossing inside one struct, and the allocator would not have bounded the struct anyway -- and this run cannot tell which. It establishes that the case runs to its defect in a Capstone domain on both arms with no fault anywhere; the 'no allocation-granular bound can see it' claim rests on the CHECKs. Build note: the driver's two aligned_alloc(64, ...) arenas are compiled as malloc, because the application SDK has no aligned_alloc (musl's fallback drags a second malloc into the link); pool-allocator.c aligns every payload from its address, so nothing relies on the arena's alignment. CAPACITY: the driver takes 80 MiB of arenas (FF2_PAYLOAD_BYTES 64 MiB + FF2_META_BYTES 16 MiB), more than the plain corpora's SDKs hold, and the first run on those refused every case at the driver's own allocation check (CONTROL-FAILED 604, recorded, not scored). These rows come from an SDK pair that differs from that one ONLY in heap capacity: level0 arena 128 MiB; Sublet pool 2^27 in a 256 MiB grant.  Fixed run of the same image: VERDICT FIXED, exit 0. Arm: the level0 heap: malloc narrows the returned capability to exactly the bytes requested (CAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS), and free only marks the block free. controls in the same boot: one-past-the-end write CAUGHT (cause=7 pc=0xc8f0e5b8 address=0xc8f51768), use-after-free read RETURNED, clean access RETURNED. Image b3d200b39acc9435. Predicted before the run (pre-registration 60f1c5be25a5); the prediction held.
spatial.prediction: PREDICTED: the sequence completes. The crossing is interior to one allocation, which the case asserts on the offsets, so a per-allocation bound is in bounds for it. NOT YET MEASURED: this corpus has no capstone-domain runner; cases 0-2 got their reading from probe cases 40-42 of ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/security-tests, and the same seam is where these will be measured. ARENA CAVEAT, stated rather than left implicit: this corpus's driver hands the port's av_malloc ONE arena (shared/driver.c calls ff2_memory_init on an aligned_alloc) and src/shared/metadata-allocator.c:26 carves it by bumping a cursor, returning a raw interior pointer and rounding every request up to 64 bytes. __builtin_capstone_cap_shrink appears only in src/capstone-domain/payload-capabilities.c:57, on pool PAYLOAD blocks. So on this harness there is NO per-allocation bound on the struct at all, and a completion here is weaker evidence than 'the bound is the whole allocation' would be. The sub-object claim does not depend on that -- the crossing is interior by construction, which the case asserts on the offsets -- but the arm must not be read as a measured per-allocation bound.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-06 on this host, revocation ON: the sequence COMPLETES on both arms and each prints its own VERDICT, so the completion is a reading and not a silent pass. NOT CAUGHT. 22 of 22 arms passed, runner exit 0, with the platform controls firing in the SAME boot: cheribsd-abi reported `CHERI_ABI pointer_bytes=16 runtime_revocation=1` and cheribsd-bounds reported CHERI_BOUNDARY_READY. THE REASON IS WEAKER THAN 'CHERI BOUNDS THE ALLOCATION AND THE CROSSING STAYS INSIDE', and that is stated rather than glossed: this corpus's driver hands the port's av_malloc ONE arena (ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/src/shared/metadata-allocator.c:26 bumps a cursor and returns a raw interior pointer, rounding every request to 64 bytes), so there is no per-allocation bound on the struct at all on this harness. The completion shows that nothing bounded anything at this granularity, not that a bound was in force and held. The sub-object claim does not rest on the arm -- the case asserts its own offsets. This is the over-claim that was corrected on the wmem arms, written down before it could be made again. BUILD: clang -O0, purecap, linked against the port's libffmpeg-pool.a from `cmake --preset cheribsd`. -O0 IS LOAD-BEARING: a first suite built -O1 returned VERDICT INCONCLUSIVE for case 0 while the other nineteen arms passed and both controls fired, because case 0's index is a compile-time constant one past its member and clang folded the store away. Rebuilt at -O0 with nothing else changed, it reads DEFECT-REPRODUCED. Reporting the -O1 suite would have recorded a compiler artifact as a CheriBSD reading. Evidence: results/20261006-cheribsd/.

native-detect.oracle: MEASURED two-sided 2026-10-06, results/20261006-native-subobject-7/: NO ASan report, and the arm also prints the value it crossed into, so the silence is not the access failing to happen. The positive control fires in the same probe: asan-probe-7.c's 'past' arm, one uint32 past the whole allocation, reports heap-buffer-overflow and exits 1. Built -O0, which is load-bearing -- at -O1 the dead stores are optimised away and the control cannot fire. The probe allocates with plain malloc rather than the port's arena, deliberately: inside a case binary av_malloc carves one arena, so ASan could not see an allocation bound even in principle and a silence there would prove nothing. DETECTOR NOTE: the first run of this probe read as a detection on ALL arms because it grepped for the string 'AddressSanitizer' while the probe leaked, and LeakSanitizer's summary line contains that string. Keyed on heap-buffer-overflow and with the leak fixed, the reading inverts. Recorded because a positive finding from a mis-keyed check is the mirror of a clean zero.

nested_why: nothing sub-allocated the crossed region: the object is one allocation the platform or FFmpeg's own av_malloc handed out directly, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT NESTED.
fault_sites_why: the defective copy is ff2_strlcpy's `memcpy(dst, src, n)` (case.c:33) with n = the SOURCE length instead of the destination size, writing past key_uri into key_string; A library function is weaker evidence than a labelled probe -- any memcpy would match, and this image has many: the buffer-pool core's av_refstruct_unref (refstruct.c:129, :132), which the case itself calls twice (case.c:111-112), av_buffer_realloc and stdio among them. (CORRECTED 2026-10-11: this sentence used to say 'it is the case's only memcpy and the buffer-pool core linked into the image calls none', which the claim audit refuted.) The attribution rests instead on three things: the fault address lies in the heap object the copy writes, not in a stream buffer or the stack; the paired fixed run of the same image, which differs only in the size argument, completes; and the supervised CheriBSD run (R3c) names memcpy's caller from its return address, ff2_strlcpy+0x7e, the instruction after the case's own call -- valid there because memcpy is a leaf. Declared 2026-10-10 from the source, before the capstone-subobject re-run that replaces the arm's old accept-anywhere waiver.
